commendation_quotes.nominator: David L. Martens, Chief, Lakeville Police Department
commendation_quotes.headline_outcome: 12 stolen firearms recovered, $25,000+ in property recovered, 75% reduction in burglary rate Q1 2001
commendation_quotes.verbatim_short: Officer Hokanson did an outstanding job creating a computer matrix representation of a very complex residential burglary/forgery case that tracked checks and losses at various locations throughout the metro area. This graphic representation not only assisted investigators in piecing the cases together, but also assisted the Officer of the County Attorney in presenting the case for charging.
commendation_quotes.verbatim_attribution_notes: Investigator after investigator commented on Troy's work ethic and spirit of cooperation. Comments such as 'positive attitude,' and 'he accurately assessed the information and took the case to the next level,' became Officer Hokanson's benchmark.

commendation_quotes.headline_outcome: Two-year multi-jurisdictional investigation, federal grand jury, 12-count indictment
commendation_quotes.verbatim_short: After approximately two years and countless hours of investigation, a grand jury was convened. The federal indictment, which consists of 12 counts, was brought against the suspect. With the joint cooperation of local, state and federal authorities, the case was brought to a successful resolution.
commendation_quotes.verbatim_attribution_notes: Task force consisted of FBI, US Postal Inspection Service, MSP International Police Department, Minnesota BCA, plus Apple Valley, Burnsville, and Eagan PDs.

commendation_quotes.headline_outcome: Multi-year commercial burglary case at Goodfellas Pizza closed with 2nd Degree Burglary guilty plea via fingerprint and Google account search warrant evidence
commendation_quotes.verbatim_short: Detective Hokanson's persistence, tenacity and hard work lead to a successful prosecution. This investigation also provided confidence in the Lakeville Police Department for a local business.
commendation_quotes.verbatim_attribution_notes: Case spanned September 29, 2016 to February 14, 2019. Detective Hokanson reviewed reports, made contact with the business owner, recovered the stolen lockbox in Savage MN, photographed and collected fingerprints from the recovered item, submitted prints to the BCA lab, then executed a search warrant on the suspect's Google account to confirm identity. The suspect ultimately pled guilty to 2nd Degree Burglary.

commendation_quotes.headline_outcome: Identified an organized criminal element conducting fraud across the Twin Cities, with $6,100 in cash and similar fraud complaints across Plymouth and Maple Grove. Suspect jailed for Theft by Swindle and Aggravated Forgery.
commendation_quotes.verbatim_short: In recognition of your initiative and actions demonstrating outstanding work to identify an organized criminal element performing fraud in the Twin Cities and bringing credibility to our Department.
commendation_quotes.verbatim_attribution_notes: Detectives Hokanson and Williams (with SRO Jensen and others) developed a controlled meet plan, apprehended the suspect, and confirmed the suspect was part of an organized crew running similar fraud across the Twin Cities. Officers seized over $6,100 in cash.

email_quotes.nominator: Chief David L. Martens, Lakeville Police Department
email_quotes.verbatim_short: I know as well as anyone that statistics do not make the officer, but I also know that they do help reflect the individual both as an officer and a person. I wanted to let the four of you know that after reviewing your most recent performance evaluations that we do appreciate your go-gettum attitude and work ethic. It is not antithetical to community oriented policing to be aggressive enforcers of the law, indeed, that is exactly what the community tells me they want out of their police. Keep up the good work.
email_quotes.verbatim_attribution_notes: Chief Martens addressed this to four officers including Troy Hokanson (badge 4849) after a quarterly performance evaluation review. The original email contained an exclamation point at the end which has been replaced with a period for voice-standard compliance.

email_quotes.nominator: Captain John Arvidson, Lakeville Police Department (relaying Sgt. Jason Polinski)
email_quotes.verbatim_short: Nice job by Troy and his trainee for being proactive and understanding that a stop for a minor violation can result in a major arrest. Also important in the message is that FTO Hokanson is instilling in our new employees a strong work ethic which includes being proactive and aggressive in enforcement of all traffic laws.
email_quotes.verbatim_attribution_notes: Sgt. Polinski's underlying message documented that Troy and his trainee turned a minor traffic stop into a controlled-buy investigation, escalating the case to a first-degree controlled substance sale with a residential search warrant and a Confidential Reliable Informant. The case produced a first-degree sale and possession charge.

email_quotes.nominator: Captain John Arvidson, Lakeville Police Department
email_quotes.verbatim_short: Nice job on the training yesterday. I know we can be a tough group to instruct.
email_quotes.verbatim_attribution_notes: Captain Arvidson addressed this to Troy and four other officers (Hvinden, Haider, Stewart, Gerl) following an internal training session they co-delivered. Demonstrates Troy's adjunct-faculty fluency carrying over into department instruction.

email_quotes.nominator: Sgt. Andy Bohlen and Chief Thomas Vonhof, Lakeville Police Department
email_quotes.verbatim_short: Thank you for representing us so well. Great work. In 1990, when I went off to active duty, my department sent marked squads to escort our company from the Austin city limits to the Rochester armory. It choked me up back then so I know your actions inspired the troops today.
email_quotes.verbatim_attribution_notes: Troy organized a 15-squad escort for SSG Ron Hvinden's 34th MP Company from the Stillwater Armory to MSP Airport. Participating agencies included Minnesota State Patrol, Stillwater PD, Minneapolis PD (with two SWAT vans), Bloomington PD, West Hennepin Public Safety, and the US Marshal's Service. Airport PD escorted the unit onto the tarmac. Chief Vonhof added: A sentiment shared by us all. This entry demonstrates Troy's military-LE bridge identity and multi-agency coordination skill.

email_quotes.nominator: Sgt. Steven Klehr, Lakeville Police Department
email_quotes.verbatim_short: Officer Hokanson obtained statements from victim, witnesses and the suspect who admitted to breaking in, pulled the phone off the wall and stealing the purse. Nice work done by Officer Hokanson.
email_quotes.verbatim_attribution_notes: Case 09-1085 involved a residential break-in at 11311 178th Street where the suspect made entry through a window, interfered with the victim's 911 call, and stole the victim's purse. Suspect located by St. Paul PD and jailed. Troy closed the case with a full suspect confession and complete victim and witness statements.

email_quotes.subject_line: Deputy Marshal Tom Knutson Letter from Chief Vonhof
email_quotes.nominator: Chief Thomas Vonhof, Lakeville Police Department
email_quotes.verbatim_short: Great job on recognizing Tom's work, good idea to send a letter to the US Marshal. I edited it a little and sent it out today.
email_quotes.verbatim_attribution_notes: Troy drafted a recognition letter from Chief Vonhof to the United States Marshal's Service acknowledging Deputy US Marshal Tom Knutson's work on case file 11002911. The Chief adopted the letter with light edits and sent it on department letterhead. Demonstrates Troy's instinct to formalize interagency relationships.

email_quotes.nominator: Sgt. Jason Polinski, Lakeville Police Department
email_quotes.verbatim_short: Wanted you all to know how much Andy and I appreciate your willingness and understanding when it pertains to this past month. As you know, a shift in the way LPD has been doing things has occurred to include a more proactive approach to the way LPD conducts business. When the change was presented to you, there was no complaining, but rather a feeling of respect towards Andy and me with what we were asking you to do. Each of you stepped up to the plate and made the change without hesitation.
email_quotes.verbatim_attribution_notes: Sgt. Polinski addressed this to Troy and the rest of the shift following a departmental shift in operating model toward more proactive enforcement. Demonstrates Troy's adaptability and constructive response to leadership change.

email_quotes.subject_line: Lakeville Police Chief's Award of Merit Presentation
email_quotes.nominator: Chief Thomas E. Vonhof, Lakeville Police Department
email_quotes.verbatim_short: Officer Hokanson nominated an off-duty civilian nurse for the Lakeville Police Department's Chief's Award of Merit for her quick response in providing lifesaving actions.
email_quotes.verbatim_attribution_notes: Troy authored and submitted the formal nomination that the Chief presented at City Council on July 16, 2012. The nomination recognized an off-duty nurse who provided immediate civilian assistance at a community pool incident. Demonstrates Troy's instinct to formalize and elevate civilian heroism through official department channels. The case content itself falls outside PTSD-safe scope and should never be described in any document, only the nomination work is citable.

email_quotes.nominator: Sgt. Jason Polinski, Lakeville Police Department (to Captain Knutson and Chief Vonhof)
email_quotes.verbatim_short: Troy and Sandy, I have been involved in starting a few new assignments at the PD over the past, and the first two officers selected for a new program are the single factor for a program working or failing. You two were selected because you two possess the skill set to make an impact and work hard for success of a new program. I am trying to say thank you and you both are doing a great job.
email_quotes.verbatim_attribution_notes: Sgt. Polinski forwarded this to senior command summarizing the success of the LPD Probation Liaison Program. Troy and Officer Sandy Thoeny were the inaugural two officers selected to build the relationship between Lakeville PD and Dakota County Probation. The forwarded thread included Dakota County Probation Officer a Dakota County probation officer's note (You do good work) confirming the partnership was producing results. The original email contained one exclamation point which has been replaced with a period for voice-standard compliance.

email_quotes.nominator: a Dakota County probation officer, Dakota County Probation Officer
email_quotes.verbatim_short: You do good work. Thanks.
email_quotes.verbatim_attribution_notes: Sent by Dakota County Probation Officer a Dakota County probation officer to Officer Sandy Thoeny regarding the joint Lakeville PD and Dakota County Probation Liaison effort with Troy and Sandy. While the named addressee was Sandy, the message acknowledged the joint Troy and Sandy partnership and was forwarded by Sgt. Polinski to senior command as the underlying validation that the new program was working. Treated as a civilian-agency partner quote because the probation partner is a Dakota County employee, not a Lakeville PD employee.

email_quotes.nominator: Detective David Watson, Lakeville Police Department
email_quotes.verbatim_short: Good job Troy.
email_quotes.verbatim_attribution_notes: Detective Watson responded to Troy's update that Intensive Supervised Release Officer Nick Sandquist had reported the subject pled guilty to a parole violation and would return to prison for one year. Demonstrates Troy's ongoing partnership with state probation and parole.

email_quotes.nominator: Chief Thomas Vonhof, Lakeville Police Department
email_quotes.verbatim_short: Perfect. Thanks Troy.
email_quotes.verbatim_attribution_notes: Chief Vonhof's acknowledgement of Troy's arrest report for a 1st Degree DWI (the suspect's fifth DWI since February 2005, captured on a scooter that ran into a parked vehicle). Forfeiture paperwork served. Demonstrates Troy's habit of looping the Chief in on notable enforcement outcomes.

email_quotes.nominator: Sgt. Jay Castonguay, Lakeville Police Department
email_quotes.verbatim_short: I just wanted to send a quick thank you for doing your own follow up on this fraud report. I believe most patrol officers would have simply forwarded it on to Investigations in the hopes it got looked into. Thanks for sparing them and taking the necessary steps to resolve this type of case on your own. Keep up the good work.
email_quotes.verbatim_attribution_notes: Sgt. Castonguay sent this directly to Troy with copies to all sergeants and staff after Troy resolved fraud case 13-4539 on his own rather than handing it off to Investigations. This entry is prime SIU and analyst material, it speaks directly to fraud-case ownership and the willingness to carry an investigation through to closure. The original email contained one exclamation point which has been replaced with a period for voice-standard compliance.

email_quotes.nominator: Sgt. Jay Castonguay, Lakeville Police Department
email_quotes.verbatim_short: Quite the documentation on his first week and uniform acquisitions. I have printed a copy of these and will place them in his FTO book. Great job and thank you for the detailed accounting.
email_quotes.verbatim_attribution_notes: Sgt. Castonguay acknowledged Troy's detailed documentation of new officer Nick Jacobson's zero-week training and uniform issue. Troy proposed building a standing uniform issue list to formalize the process. Demonstrates Troy's adjunct-faculty instinct for documentation and process formalization.

email_quotes.nominator: Chief Jeffrey Long, Lakeville Police Department
email_quotes.verbatim_short: It was great to hear about the work you had done on the the federal case subject case with the Postal Inspectors Office. Considering much of my background was in Investigations, I sincerely enjoyed hearing about this case. Although the investigations can seem long and mundane, in the end, a bad lady will be going to jail for a long time. Thanks for the work that you do and congrats on the commendations you received.
email_quotes.verbatim_attribution_notes: Chief Long acknowledged Troy's work on the joint Lakeville PD and US Postal Inspection Service investigation involving subject the federal case subject. Troy later received a formal award from the US Postal Inspection Service for his work on this case, the Chief's email also referenced commendations Troy had already received. This entry is high-value, the federal partnership and USPIS award are concrete external recognition. The original email contained one exclamation point which has been replaced with a period for voice-standard compliance.

email_quotes.nominator: Lt. William Gerl, Lakeville Police Department (relaying Daniel Brettschneider, Recreation Program Supervisor)
email_quotes.verbatim_short: Thanks for handling this Troy and representing us well. I will place a copy of this email in your station file.
email_quotes.verbatim_attribution_notes: Lt. Gerl acknowledged Troy's outreach work at the city's Little Tykes Safety Camp and placed the recognition in Troy's station file. The forwarded note from Recreation Program Supervisor Daniel Brettschneider said Troy did an awesome job with the kids. Demonstrates community-facing teaching ability outside of pure enforcement work.

email_quotes.nominator: a Lakeville resident, Lakeville resident
email_quotes.verbatim_short: I would like to thank Officers Troy Hokanson and Mike Lamm for checking out the situation and helping my family member feel safe. They handled the situation professionally and with caution to get the correct story. It was reassuring to me and my family that we could count on the Lakeville Police.
email_quotes.verbatim_attribution_notes: Lakeville resident a Lakeville resident wrote directly to Chief Jeff Long and Sgt. Steve Klehr after Troy and Officer Lamm responded to a possible stolen-property exchange involving a family member's stolen property (case [case file redacted] from Burnsville PD). Troy and Lamm met the involved parties at the a local commercial location, gathered statements, and ensured her family member's safety. The original letter contained two exclamation points which have been replaced with periods for voice-standard compliance. This is a strong citizen quote for any cover letter targeting community-facing or fraud-recovery work.

email_quotes.nominator: Sgt. Bradley Paulson, Lakeville Police Department
email_quotes.verbatim_short: Nice job by Officers Hokanson and Wubben.
email_quotes.verbatim_attribution_notes: Sgt. Paulson's shift summary entry for case 16-000954 documented Troy initiating a vehicle stop that escalated when the driver fled. Troy initiated the pursuit with Officer Wubben assisting. The pursuit was terminated at the city edge once the driver was positively identified, with a KOPS Alert issued for the vehicle and probable cause established for Felony Flee Police in a Motor Vehicle. Quote isolated to Troy's case only, the broader shift summary contains unrelated case content that falls outside PTSD-safe scope and should not be quoted.

email_quotes.nominator: Chief Jeffrey Long, Lakeville Police Department
email_quotes.verbatim_short: The leaders of self-initiated activity, month after month, such as Doyle Cockrell, Nick Jacobson, Troy Hokanson, Todd Williams, Alison Shank and Scott Frame make hundreds of traffic stops and rarely, if ever, get any complaints. That is very impressive. When I started here close to three years ago, I challenged the senior employees to lead the way in self-initiated activity while on patrol shifts. I owe Doyle, Todd, and Troy a great deal of thanks for doing so.
email_quotes.verbatim_attribution_notes: Chief Long sent this to the entire LPD staff. Troy was named among the top self-initiated-activity leaders, a category the Chief had specifically challenged senior employees to lead in. The Chief noted that this group made hundreds of traffic stops with rarely any complaints, demonstrating respect-based policing and professionalism.

email_quotes.nominator: Officer Thomas Stewart, Lakeville Police Department (with Lt. Jason Polinski concurrence)
email_quotes.verbatim_short: Thank you ALL for your help with this case from start to finish. SRO Thor, SRO Stevens, Detective Jensen, Detective Hokanson, and DTF Agent Thoeny stayed at the PD hours after their shift ended to help me with interviews, vehicle search, inventory, property, warrants, and paper work. Awesome job and thank you all again.
email_quotes.verbatim_attribution_notes: Officer Stewart thanked the team that helped close case 16005045 in which an OSINT-driven investigation began with the suspect displaying a recently obtained handgun on Facebook. The team executed a coordinated stop, vehicle search warrant, and inventory that recovered the handgun as confirmed stolen from Lakeville's jurisdiction. Lt. Polinski added Wow, nice work on this everyone. Demonstrates Troy's OSINT awareness, after-hours commitment, and willingness to assist across detective, SRO, and DTF units. The original emails contained exclamation points which have been replaced with periods for voice-standard compliance.
